_comment: Every binary FoodTruck installs for its own use, pinned by digest.
This file is the SBOM. One place to review, one diff to audit, and a
mismatch discards the download and changes nothing.
It is read from inside the SIGNED APP BUNDLE, never from the writable
pantry. A user may fork a recipe -- that is the point of the pantry -- but
a forked recipe must not be able to repoint a download at another host.
'provenance' is not decoration: it records what integrity guarantee the
upstream actually offers, so a reviewer can see where the trust ends.
'verify' is the command that re-derives the digest from upstream, so
`foodtruck lint pins` can prove these values still match.

artifacts.provenance: go-task publishes task_checksums.txt but no signature and no attestation (verified: the attestations API returns 404, .goreleaser.yml has no signs: block). This digest is the only integrity anchor available.

jdx/mise publishes SHASUMS256.txt per release and a GPG signature for install.sh (key 24853EC9F655CE80B48E6C3A8B81C9D17413A06D). We pin the release archive digest directly, which avoids trusting the install script at all.
